## What stands out

- **`co2_ppm` is never missing** — 0 of 821 monthly rows, 0 of 67 annual. NOAA fills gaps by interpolation. The three *quality* columns (`num_days`, `std_dev`, `uncertainty`) are missing for ~195 rows: every month before May 1974 (that stretch is Scripps data, without daily-count statistics) plus interpolated months.
- **It only goes up.** For `co2-annual-mlo` the min (315.98) is the first year and the max (427.35) is the last. For `co2-growth-annual`, `mlo_ppm_per_year` has a minimum of **0.31** — the CO₂ annual mean has not fallen once in 67 years.
- **The rise is accelerating.** Mean annual growth is 1.68 ppm/yr over the whole record, but `co2-growth-decadal` runs from 0.86 (1960s) to 2.56 (2010s).
- **The Mauna Loa uncertainty columns carry no information.** `uncertainty` in `co2-annual-mlo` is 0.12 for every row (std dev 0); `mlo_uncertainty` is a flat 0.11. NOAA publishes one figure, not a per-year estimate. The *global* uncertainties do vary (0.03–0.10; 0.05–0.34).
- **Two decadal rows are partial.** `co2-growth-decadal.n_years` has a minimum of 1 — the 1950s and the current 2020s cover fewer than ten years, so their means are noisier than the rest.
